title: WHY ARE YOU CRYING OUT?
paragraphs: WHY ARE YOU CRYING OUT?

The sea was in front of them.
Pharaoh was behind them.
And panic was louder than faith.

Israel did what scared people do.
They cried.
They blamed.
They forgot.

Exodus 14 is not just a miracle story.
It is the x-ray of the human heart.
When pressure rises, fear starts preaching.

“Was it because there were no graves in Egypt?”
That’s what they said. Not prayer. Not trust. Panic with a voice.
And then God answers Moses with a question that cuts through the noise:

“Why are you crying out to Me? Tell the Israelites to move on.”
—Exodus 14:15
That line burns.

Because there comes a moment when heaven says:
Enough trembling.
Lift the staff.
Step forward.
Watch Me work.

Moses raised his staff, but the power was never in the wood.
The power was in the God who rules wind, water, armies, and timelines.
One lifted hand.
One command from God.
And the impossible split open.

Fear said, “You’re trapped.”
God said, “Make a path.”

That is what human fear never understands:
when God leads you to the edge, He is not setting you up for destruction.
He is setting the stage for revelation.

Some of you are standing at your own Red Sea right now.
Bills rising.
Family breaking.
Old chains chasing you.
Eyes full of tears.
Heart full of noise.
Hear the Word of the Lord:

Stop letting fear narrate your future.
The same God who brought you out knows how to bring you through.
But don’t miss the deeper miracle.

Israel was not only being rescued from Egypt.
They were being separated from it.
God didn’t just open water.
He closed the door on slavery.
That points us straight to Jesus.

Because humanity had a greater Pharaoh: sin.
A deeper bondage: guilt.
A darker enemy: death.

And at the cross, Jesus stepped into the place we could not survive.
He made a way where there was no way.
Not through a sea of water—
but through judgment, wrath, and the grave.

By His blood, the chains break.
By His resurrection, the path opens.
By His grace, your past does not get the final word.

So yes—cry if you must.
But don’t camp in fear.
Raise what God placed in your hand.
Obey the next instruction.
Move when He says move.

The sea does not decide your story.
God does.
And when He makes a way, no enemy can unmake it.
Jesus still turns trapped people into testimony.

Repent.
Trust Christ.
Walk forward.
